subject: Erase window vs model-learning guarantee — follow-up on retention and attestations
messages:

Cc: procurement@havenhealth.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on erase window vs ML training guarantee

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the infra performance looked good. Legal and procurement are asking for a short write-up on two specific points before we can move the PO forward: (1) your erase/soft-delete timeline (what exactly happens when we request deletion), and (2) an explicit statement that data submitted to the hosted API will not be used to train Redwood models under the default contract (and, if there are exceptions, what they are).

We need a short explanation we can attach to our privacy review and a formal attestation we can share with our SOC team. High level is fine, but include any TL;DR retention windows for logs, debug snapshots, backups, and whether redacted/aggregated telemetry could ever flow into training. Also flag any cases where customer opt-in would make data eligible for training.

Appreciate a quick response — procurement is hoping to close the week.

Cheers,
Elena
Elena Morales
Legal Ops | Haven Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Hi Elena — thanks for the concise ask and great to meet yesterday. Below is a short, actionable summary you can use for procurement and SOC; I’ve looped in Marissa (CS) and Priyom from Legal for a formal attestation PDF and a retention matrix.

TL;DR (for inclusion in your packet):
- Redwood does not use customer-provided request payloads or generated outputs to train our models by default.
- Data retention windows: soft-delete tombstone is immediate (data becomes inaccessible for serving), standard debug snapshots are retained up to 30 days for incident investigation, backups/snapshots for disaster recovery can be held up to 90 days but are encrypted and access-controlled, and operational telemetry (latency/aggregate usage) is retained in aggregated form and not tied to raw customer text.
- Exceptions: the only way customer text would be used for training is if a customer explicitly opts-in via a documented, auditable consent process (e.g., program participation). Any such program is opt-in, time-bound, and subject to additional contractual terms.
- We provide an attestation letter and a retention matrix (see attachments) for SOC2 review.

More context:
- Deletion: when you request data erasure for a customer (API key/tenant), we initiate an erasure workflow. First, tokens and request payloads are marked deleted and removed from live serving caches (prefix/KV caches). Indexed metadata used for routing is tombstoned immediately. For backups and debug snapshots, we maintain a documented tombstone lifecycle: snapshot records are flagged and queued for secure purging; those queued copies are overwritten or shredded within the windows above unless a legal hold is in place.
- Training: model training uses curated datasets that are segregated from customer tenants. We segregate training pipelines from production inference logs; production raw payloads are never fed into training without explicit opt-in. Aggregated metrics (e.g., 95th percentile latency, per-model token counts) are retained for product improvement but cannot be reverse-engineered to recover customer payloads.

I’m attaching a short spec and the retention matrix; Priyom will follow up with formal attestation language for signatures. Let me know if you want tighter TTLs or an SLA clause — we can propose a shorter snapshot window as part of the contract if needed.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: No-Model-Training-Spec.pdf (overview), erase-window-matrix.xlsx (retention windows, internal use)

Subject: Re: Question on erase window vs ML training guarantee

Hi Elena,

Following up with formal language you can drop into vendor intake: we will provide a signed attestation that, under the terms of the proposed MSA, Redwood will not use customer-provided text or generated outputs to train models unless the customer has provided explicit, documented opt-in consent.

Operational clarifications we typically include in the attestation:
- "Data in scope for the attestation": API request payloads, real-time streaming inputs, and generated responses.
- "Excluded from the attestation": anonymized/aggregated telemetry necessary for service stability and product diagnostics; these metrics are never reversible to customer text.
- "Erasure process": initiation, tombstoning of live copies, purge schedule for snapshots and backups (30/90 default), and an escalation path for legal holds.

If Haven Health needs a shorter snapshot window (e.g., 7 days) we can include a contractual statement and operational runbook; that change will require a small operational configuration on our side (we log it and apply for the tenant).

I'll attach a draft attestation in PDF for signature and a cleaned retention matrix for your packet. If your SOC team prefers, we can add an explicit line about non-derivative claims (i.e., we do not train derivative models using your data).

Regards,
Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks Priyom and Jonas — that language is precisely what we need. Two quick asks before we close: (1) include an explicit line in the attestation that debug snapshots retained for investigations are encrypted-at-rest and accessible only to a named on-call SRE group (we'll accept role-based description rather than a personnel list), and (2) please add a brief bullet that confirms aggregated telemetry is processed through a noise/aggregation pipeline prior to any product analytics so it cannot be used to reconstruct text.

If those two bullets are in the PDF we'll be able to attach and move the PO. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Elena
